validation.value: Near-unity factors judged implausible; motivates chemical-feasibility modelling

evidence.quote: As it is unlikely that the gas completely fills the beam in all sub-regions these values suggest the conditions found to be incorrect, likely as a result of the models not considering the chemical feasibility of the parameters.

method.value: Free-fall collapse followed by fixed-density heating and evolution; convert chemical abundances and extinction to CS column density; pass physical conditions and column density to RADEX.

evidence.quote: The first stage allows the cloud to collapse by free-fall until it reaches a specified density, in order to create a high density cloud with self consistent abundances.
In the second stage the collapse is halted such that the density remains constant and a burst of star formation is simulated by heating the gas up to a specified temperature.

referee_caveats_inferred: The listed chemical-grid dimensions imply 108 combinations, whereas the paper states 36 models; the actual run selection is unresolved.
The abstract reports hydrogen volume densities in cm^-2, while the modelling sections and conclusions use cm^-3.
The introductory common-resolution description needs reconciliation with the explicit statement that only ratio maps use convolved images.
Ad hoc χ² contour multipliers are not stated confidence intervals.
A posteriori filling factors do not propagate their covariance with excitation and chemical parameters.
The externally imposed 50 K RADEX bound should not be treated as a measured CS temperature.
Coarse-grid temperatures, ionisation rates and proposed shock chemistry are weaker answer keys than directly measured line intensities.
